evidence: No incompatible-product pair was found, but several scored observables are graded in two criteria, and one criterion subsumes another. The functional judge.toml claims at line 35 that 'Each observable is graded in exactly one criterion', and these overlaps contradict that. (1) Transcript reply threading is graded twice. .qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r4/task/tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:244 (search_and_transcript Part B leg 2) says 'Messages are oldest first and in their threads: JUDGE-T1 sits under JUDGE-T0', and line 246 fails it 'if any ... thread placement ... is wrong'. .qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r4/task/tests/scored/polish/judge.toml:48-54 (transcript_print) asks the judge to 'Confirm each reply is clearly shown as part of the thread it answers, by its placement or by a visible reply-to label'. Any transcript that passes the functional leg also passes the polish criterion, so polish adds no separate credit, and an unthreaded transcript fails both. (2) The timer placement beside the title is graded twice. .qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r4/task/tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:130 (timer_changes leg 1) requires that 'the thread shows 7 days beside the title', and line 135 fails it 'if the 7-day setting is not shown'. .qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r4/task/tests/scored/polish/judge.toml:20-27 (timer_label) separately requires the setting to 'sit next to the matter title and [be] read at a glance, without opening a menu'. (3) Each transcript message's sent time is graded twice. .qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r4/task/tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:216-217 (sent_once_in_order Part B) requires '2026-05-12 11:00 in the transcript' and fails if 'any of them shows a different sent time'. .qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r4/task/tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:244/246 (search_and_transcript B2) requires 'each message shows its author and sent time' and fails if the 'time ... is wrong or missing'. (4) There are lesser overlaps. .qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r4/task/tests/scored/polish/judge.toml:39-45 (phone_matter, scrollWidth equals viewport and the box is reachable) overlaps .qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r4/task/tests/scored/visual/judge.toml:69-81 (phone_chambers, whose 2 anchor is 'text clipped or box off screen'). Deleted text being absent from search or the transcript is re-checked in deleted_and_expired_messages, timer_changes and hold_scope_and_release. Reply nesting is required in nested_replies, live_updates_keep_my_work ('JUDGE-LR appears under JUDGE-LB', .qc-cache/kittle-2026-10-09-r4/task/tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:228) and deleted_and_expired_messages. These lesser cases cover distinct deletion and live-update promises in a shared scenario, so on their own they are Notes, not the blocking defect. (5) Positive controls that repeat another criterion's feature are required by check 30 and REVIEW_POLICY, so I do not count them as defects. The link preview in wall_mentions_and_links (line 72) repeats message_links, and the wrong-password refusal appears in the render gate, signin_and_client_scope and polish refusal_in_place. The gate overlap has zero weight. (6) I checked the criteria against each other for incompatible demands or destructive state hand-offs and found none. timer_changes shortens M-13 to 7 days, which deletes only K-13 (4 May), while K-8 'Draft will sent for your review.' (10 May) survives for message_links and live_updates. The timer is restored to 30. Walls added in wall_added_live and persistence are lifted, and M-12's timer is restored to off, matching the seed's null. Refusal wording is consistent: a wall or out-of-scope request gets a plain not-available, and timer_changes leg 2 explicitly allows not-available, an error or an empty list for a deleted message's versions. This is a source-level structural check, and no runtime measurement is needed to establish the overlap.
counterexample: Take an app that is otherwise conforming but renders its transcript as a flat chronological list with no indentation and no reply-to labels. It loses search_and_transcript (weight 2.5 of 33, which also forfeits its Part A search credit) and polish transcript_print (1 of 5). That costs about 0.045 + 0.04 of reward for one defect. Similarly, an app that shows the disappearing timer only inside a header menu fails timer_changes (2.0 of 33, forfeiting its deletion, hold-survival and associate-refusal credit) and polish timer_label. An app whose transcript omits per-message sent times fails both sent_once_in_order (2.5) and search_and_transcript (2.5). In each case one observable is penalised in two criteria.
suggested_fix: Give each observable one owner. Drop the threading leg from either search_and_transcript B2 or polish transcript_print. Remove the 'shows 7 days beside the title' display leg from timer_changes and let polish timer_label own placement, keeping only the state check that the setting reads 7 days in the matter's timer display or control. Remove the transcript sent-time leg from either sent_once_in_order Part B or search_and_transcript B2. Otherwise, correct the functional judge.toml line 35 claim. Recheck coverage after the edit.
